title: InCLAD: A Continual Learning Benchmark for Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection
abstract: arXiv:2610.15032v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Industrial anomaly detection benchmarks have advanced rapidly, yet they remain largely static and therefore underrepresent deployment settings in which inspection systems must be extended from one industrial component to another over time. In our setting, continual industrial anomaly detection is framed as a task-incremental problem: each component defines a task, while the learning objective remains semi-supervised. The goal extends beyond conventional anomaly detection, since models should preserve their performance on all components as they are sequentially exposed to new components. This framing is especially relevant because many existing industrial pipelines either assume fully supervised defect labels or study only isolated datasets, leaving open the question of how semi-supervised anomaly detectors behave across a sequence of heterogeneous components. translated_title: InCLAD：面向工业视觉异常检测的持续学习基准
translated_abstract: 工业异常检测基准近年来发展迅速，但它们在很大程度上仍然是静态的，因此未能充分反映检测系统需要随时间从一个工业组件扩展到另一个组件的实际部署场景。在我们的设定中，持续工业异常检测被构建为一个任务增量问题：每个组件定义一个任务，而学习目标保持半监督性质。该目标超越了传统的异常检测，因为模型在依次接触新组件时，应当保持在所有组件上的性能。这一框架尤为重要，因为许多现有的工业流程要么假设拥有完全监督的缺陷标签，要么只研究孤立的数据集，从而留下了半监督异常检测器在一系列异构组件上表现如何这一悬而未决的问题。我们通过将该基准组织为一系列相关组件的序列（摘要在此处截断）来填补这一空白。
tldr: 该论文提出了InCLAD，一个面向工业视觉异常检测的持续学习基准，将检测任务构建为任务增量的半监督学习问题，用于评估模型在依次学习新工业组件的同时保持已有组件性能的能力。
